It is not. No prohibited file was opened.

counterExample.statedAlgorithm: sha256("opensip.evidence.universe.v1" || length-prefixed sorted member keys joined), memberIdentity = evaluationId + "\x1f" + predicateId
counterExample.result: NOT REPRODUCIBLE. Six plausible framings tried (separator \x1f and |, cross u32be / u64le / no length prefix). None reproduces the fixture value sha256:5bf078b03a2a9e89. The artifact's own memberIds fixtures use '|' where memberIdentity specifies \x1f, and fixture digests are 16 hex characters where SHA-256 is 64, with no stated truncation rule.

areaFindings.name: Crate/module decomposition and the host/pure-core boundary
areaFindings.detail: IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §4 gives 16 named packages with an explicit owns / must-not-own column, an expected dependency-direction tree, and five forbidden-edge classes declared as conformance tests from the first commit. §3.1 assigns every effect (worktree read, provider spawn, durable write, Run seal, D9 derivation, process exit) to the host unambiguously. R-1 v1.4 §factoring gives the reasoned split (C-2's no-effect-authority stages are exactly the pure-core stages), §capabilityBoundary.coreDepsSchema gives a closed four-field CoreDeps with an explicit seven-item forbids list and 'Any field not listed is forbidden. CoreDeps is not an open extension point.' §coreApi gives the exact signature. I could lay out the workspace, write the cargo-deny/dependency-closure test, and defend it in review without a single guess.
residualsOnly: R1-PARK-RUNTIME-DENIAL — the static closure is proven, runtime denial is NOT DISCHARGED. Pre-named.

areaFindings.name: PlanId derivation — can it be computed from what is written?
areaFindings.verdict: SUFFICIENT — the strongest artifact in the package
areaFindings.detail: Yes. I implemented CVE1 and the PLAN-ID-V1 framing from prose alone and reproduced expectedPreimageByteLength and expectedPlanId byte-exactly for the base vector and both transformation vectors, first attempt, no checker consulted. The contract supplies: exact domain bytes in hex, u16be recipe version and field count, the field frame (u8 tag || u32be length || CVE1), a closed 8-type CVE1 grammar with constraints, all 13 field tags with shape and source, per-field canonicalization rules including set-vs-sequence semantics, a closed PlanDescriptorV1 with nested closure and admissionDescriptorEquality, per-provider semantic universe schemas, and 9 negative vectors with named outcome codes. The CI layer-4 rule is enforced in the recipe itself (PLAN_ID_PROFILE_VIOLATION for a layer-4 record under ci) and I reproduced the local-interactive keyed variant.
areaFindings.oneRealCaveat: PLAN-ID-V1 field 3 requires release.capabilityManifestId, and DELIVERY supplies no derivation rule for capabilityManifestId while asserting it enters PlanId. The recipe is exact; one of its inputs is not. See ESC-22.

areaFindings.name: Fact provider interface and the Rust sidecar process boundary
areaFindings.verdict: SEVERELY ASYMMETRIC — TypeScript sufficient, Rust not reachable
areaFindings.typescript: Fully implementable. delivery.v2.json#typescriptSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.wireSchema is a closed protocol: byte-exact framing (uint64be payload length, 32 raw SHA-256 payload bytes, one canonical-CBOR payload), RFC 8949 core deterministic CBOR with a closed 9-type model and 7 forbidden constructs and an explicit map-order rule, a closed 4-field frame envelope with per-direction monotonic sequence, 7 host->worker and 9 worker->host frame types with terminal flags, 16 closed payload schemas, 11 definitions, 11 numeric limits, a 7-phase ordering FSM with cancel transitions, commitment domains with the formula SHA-256(UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || deterministic-CBOR(value)), exact argv and a closed environment spec, and the whole wireSchema object is itself digest-pinned (sha256:96ffbe7b63972c99409125d9f7c18def5a2ca20f1e00bfbc7770f1d8321ce726) so drift is detectable.
areaFindings.rust: NOT IMPLEMENTABLE from the reachable package. delivery.v2.json#rustSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol is five prose keys. frameIntegrity reads 'uint64 big-endian length plus sha256 payload digest' with no statement of whether the digest is 32 raw bytes or 64 hex characters, whether it precedes or follows the payload, or whether it is counted inside the length. 'canonical CBOR' carries no RFC reference, no closed data model, no map-ordering rule. There is no frame envelope, no frame vocabulary in either direction, no ordering state machine, no cancel path, no Unavailable/BudgetExhausted path, no limits, no supervision or environment or scratch policy — all of which exist on the TypeScript side. The handshake gives 7 field NAMES with no types. Two engineers cannot produce interoperable framing.
areaFindings.rootCause: The artifact rust-provider-protocol.v4.json (124 KB) exists and the plan's own gate table lists it as an independently reviewed load-bearing surface at PASS. It is referenced by ZERO of the four package documents and by ZERO bytes of delivery.v2.json. It is unreachable from the delivered package. See ESC-01.
areaFindings.hostSideSufficiency: The 12-relation registry, per-relation ladders, 12 closed payload schemas, FactRequirement, the closed deficiency vocabulary and its first-match-wins resolution order, and 12 sufficiency goldens are all concrete. The blocker is the 'view' input type and the rungUnavailableBecause discriminator, neither of which is declared. See ESC-17.

areaFindings.name: Evidence — what must be persisted for an authoritative Run, and in what shape
areaFindings.verdict: NOT IMPLEMENTABLE — and only partly for the pre-named V10 reason
areaFindings.preNamedPart: The proof model, retained verification/regeneration closure, retention default, availability/degradation record, and purge semantics are explicitly marked [PHASE-1A / V10 BLOCKER] in the blueprint, are UNSET-BLOCKS-FREEZE in the freeze §3, are V10 UNRESOLVED with requiredResolution in threat-model.v3.json, are G19 BLOCKED-NO-MECHANISM in operability.v2.json, and are CD-RT-5 BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A in product-dispositions.v1.json. This is correctly and consistently pre-named. I escalate it as a residual and it does not count against the litmus.
areaFindings.notPreNamedPart: Blueprint §7.2 step 6 instructs the implementer to port EVIDENCE bundle-shape accepting and rejection fixtures BEFORE the Phase-1A step 7. That instruction is not executable at evidence.v1: bundleSchema has no types, the load-bearing 'authoritative' field is missing from the schema while appearing in all 18 fixtures, seven per-evaluation fields appear only in fixtures, all fixture digests are stubs that do not match ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$, and the one concrete commitment recipe does not reproduce its own goldens. Separately, EvidenceDigest, RunId, sealed-Run manifest identity, Finding fingerprint, FactViewId and cache/regeneration keys are recorded in operability.v2.json#knownLimitations as recipes that 'do not yet exist as exact live byte contracts' — and none of those six appears in the freeze §7 named-residual table. See ESC-02 through ESC-12.
areaFindings.whatIsSufficient: The MEANING of evidence is well argued and usable: noMatchConstruction (sorted-leaf Merkle root for non-membership), verificationRequirement ('The subjectSetRoot alone is insufficient'), the three assuranceCapabilities with explicit gating, the 10 invariants E1-E10, and 5 accepting plus 13 counterexample fixtures with concrete bundles. The failure is representational, not conceptual.

areaFindings.name: Retention/custody — host obligations before the first durable write, and behavior when evidence is later unavailable
areaFindings.verdict: SPLIT — pre-write admission SUFFICIENT; later-unavailability BLOCKED (pre-named)
areaFindings.canStart: pre-write path yes; degradation path no
areaFindings.beforeFirstDurableWrite: SUFFICIENT and unusually good. threat-model.v3.json#storageNamespace.admittedStorageRoot.admission gives the exact ordering: 'Canonicalise and open the root; validate storage-root.v1.json; run exposure detectors and filesystem support checks before user-derived writes; retain the root handle for root-confined operations.' storageExposureDetectors gives a closed DETECTED/NOT-DETECTED/UNKNOWN result set, three classes, and a closed admissionDecisions table (cloud-sync-or-ci-upload DETECTED = REFUSE; permission-exposed DETECTED = REFUSE; backup-managed DETECTED = REQUIRE-EXPLICIT-POLICY-AND-DISCLOSE-EXTERNAL-COPIES; any UNKNOWN = DO-NOT-CLAIM-SAFE plus require an admitted private root), a 4-entry signed initial detector catalog, and the scoping rule that NOT-DETECTED never means globally safe. evidence.v1 E6/RA-6 independently states 'No durable user-derived write occurs before all three [storageRoot, privacyClass, retentionPolicy] are resolved.' V18 additionally requires handle revalidation on every run. The layout (12 exact paths), objectId path derivation, path-safety with handle-relative no-follow opens and an explicit 'String-prefix checks are insufficient', per-project SQLite tenancy, the single authority-selection record with compare-and-swap, and the complete purge (6 states + 6 fixtures) and migration (10 rows + 10 fixtures) crash-recovery state machines are all implementation-grade.
areaFindings.whenEvidenceLaterUnavailable: BLOCKED — and correctly pre-named. evidence.v1 E5 states 'availability is tracked externally at evidence-unit granularity' with no external mechanism defined here; E7 names 'explicit expiry or purge' with no state machine; retentionPolicy is a required field with no type or vocabulary (the fixture value 'P30D' is the only evidence it is an ISO-8601 duration); the only stated degradation semantic is the prohibition 'The no-match becomes UNVERIFIABLE. It does not silently degrade to trusted.' threat-model V10.requiredResolution item 3 is exactly 'State how purge changes current evidence availability without rewriting the sealed Run', and it is UNRESOLVED. The package is consistent and honest here; I escalate it as a residual.
areaFindings.twoStateVocabulariesNote: deletionProtocol.states (ACTIVE/PURGE-PREPARED/TOMBSTONED/PHYSICALLY-REMOVED/VERIFIED) and storageNamespace...purge.states (PREPARED/QUARANTINED/DELETE_IN_PROGRESS/VERIFIED_ABSENT/COMPLETE) do not align. Only the latter has a crash-recovery table, and deletionProtocol.scope explicitly defers to it, so the ambiguity is resolvable by reading — recorded as a nuisance, not a fork.

areaFindings.name: Termination — deriving exit class and code for a given scenario purely from the contracts
areaFindings.verdict: PARTIAL — roughly 70% derivable; the remainder forks
areaFindings.canStart: exit map and union yes; full derive no
fullyDerivable: exit_code(TerminationClass) -> i32. The 6-entry classToExitCode map is total and unambiguous (success 0, policy-failed 1, request-rejected 2, indeterminate 3, operational-failed 4, interrupted 130) and agrees with exitClasses[].code. Writable today.
HostTermination as a closed Rust enum with #[serde(tag="class")] and deny_unknown_fields. exitCode is explicitly forbidden in the payload so the two can never disagree.
The three cause-bearing classes via crossAxisInvariants X1/X2/X3 biconditionals plus total injective codeMaps.

Scenario (a) truncated Rust CBOR frame: DETERMINED. delivery.v2 terminationIntegration.providerProtocolFault -> faultCause provider-protocol -> PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION -> X3 -> operational-failed -> exit 4. Golden analysis-provider-protocol-prevents-seal confirms.

Scenario (b) required provider unavailable, coverage deficient, Run seals: DETERMINED. deficiency provider-unavailable -> COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE -> X1 -> indeterminate -> exit 3, with every axis pinned by golden analysis-required-provider-unavailable. This is the cleanest scenario in the contract.

Scenario (c) excluded capability-runtime form rejected pre-attempt: class and code DETERMINED. FEATURE.REQUIRES_CAPABILITY_RUNTIME stays domain detail; rejectionCause extension-admission-rejected -> EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED -> X2 -> request-rejected -> exit 2. The two vocabularies are explicitly declared non-interchangeable.
The concurrent-condition reducer's cross-family precedence (fault > rejection > deficiency) with a stated rationale.
44 goldenCases each with 13 fully populated scenario axes and an expected termination payload, portable as Rust table tests.
notDerivable: Scenario (d) ledger transaction fails after CAS objects were written: class operational-failed and exit 4 are determined by X3+X8, but the public errorCode is NOT. Three faultCauses fit the same physical event — durability-commit (DURABILITY.COMMIT_FAILED), cas-link (CAS.LINK_FAILED), host-io (HOST.IO_FAILURE) — and the contract gives no observation-to-cause selection rule. The maps are injective; the step before them is unwritten. See ESC-13.

When each optional union field must be populated. No predicate is given and the goldens are mutually inconsistent (analysis-durability-failed emits runId+executionId; analysis-cas-link-failed emits executionId only; query-required-completeness-missing emits coverageId with no runId). invariant-envelope-parity makes this observable, so it is not cosmetic. See ESC-14.

The rule producing success / policy-failed / interrupted. X1-X3 pin only the three cause-bearing classes; no rule anywhere states verdict==fail -> policy-failed. The normative derivation lives in artifacts/check-d9.py per referenceDerivation, i.e. outside the contract. See ESC-15.
Precedence between interrupted and policy-failed/success for a finite command. No rule, no invariant, no golden; invariant-finalization-commit hedges with 'may yield interrupted'. See ESC-16.
The shape of the request-rejected 'details' object, which DELIVERY requires to carry the domain reason code. See ESC-25.
Intra-family selection: the reducer says 'pick first faultCauses[0]' without specifying caller list order.

finalizationTransitions is 6 classes x 3 events = 18 identity rows asserting post-settlement immutability. It is not a state machine you can implement a finalizer from; the contract concedes this in knownLimitations[4].

escalations.title: The Rust provider wire protocol has no reachable normative home in the delivered package
escalations.whatINeeded: A byte-level frame format, frame vocabulary, ordering state machine, cancel path and fault taxonomy for the rustc_driver sidecar — the same class of specification the TypeScript worker receives.
escalations.whereILooked: IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §3.3 and §5 (DELIVERY row), IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §3.2 and §6.10, v1-slice.md §2.1, and delivery.v2.json#rustSemanticSubstrate.
escalations.whyInsufficient: delivery.v2.json#rustSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol is five prose keys totalling under 200 words. frameIntegrity ('uint64 big-endian length plus sha256 payload digest') does not say whether the digest is 32 raw bytes or 64 hex characters, whether it precedes or follows the payload, or whether it is inside the length. 'canonical CBOR' has no RFC reference, no closed data model and no map-ordering rule. There is no frame envelope, no message types, no sequence discipline, no terminal rules, no cancel path, no Unavailable or BudgetExhausted path, no limits. The handshake lists 7 field names with no types.
escalations.reachabilityFinding: rust-provider-protocol.v4.json (124033 bytes) exists. The string 'rust-provider-protocol' occurs 0 times in IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md, 0 in IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md, 0 in v1-slice.md, 0 in ARCHITECTURE-TO-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md, and 0 times in delivery.v2.json. Same for delivery-rust-provider-join.v* and resolved-inputs-rust-provider-join.v*. The plan's own gate table lists 'Rust provider protocol v4 — PASS', so the specification almost certainly exists and is simply orphaned from the implementer's reachable graph.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes, catastrophically. The honest move from the reachable package is to adopt the TypeScript wireSchema as the normative protocol for both sidecars — but the two sections describe different transports, different handshake field sets and different integrity phrasing, so that is a design decision the implementer would be making, not one the artifact makes. Any two engineers produce non-interoperable sidecars, and the sidecar is one of the seven areas the v1 slice requires.
escalations.fix: Add rust-provider-protocol.v4.json (and the two join artifacts) to the blueprint §5 contract map and to the freeze §2 authority set, and cross-reference it from delivery.v2.json#rustSemanticSubstrate.

escalations.title: RunId has no derivation recipe, and the freeze asserts that it does
escalations.whatINeeded: How the host allocates or derives RunId at seal, so a second process can address a sealed Run.
escalations.whereILooked: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6.6, IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §3.1, c2-plan-stage-schema.v3.json#planIntent.storedViewIntentV1, evidence.v1.json#bundleSchema, operability.v2.json, d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json, resolved-inputs.v2.json.
escalations.whyInsufficient: operability.v2.json states verbatim: 'No exact RunId derivation recipe is binding yet.' and lists 'RunId derivation' among six parked surfaces in requestIdContract.fixtures[8].parked. C-2 gives only a wire pattern (^run1:[0-9a-f]{64}$) with the explicit disclaimer 'derivation/custody remains a Run identity concern'. evidence.v1 uses the literal placeholder '$R' for runId in all 18 fixtures with no format statement. D9 references RunId as an identifier type without defining it.
escalations.conflictWithBindingArtifact: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6.6 states 'Exact SNAPSHOT-ID-V1, PLAN-ID-V1, RunId, and evidence identity keep separate descriptors, recipes, and custody.' That asserts RunId has a recipe. operability.v2.json says it does not. Per the blueprint's own rule ('If this blueprint and a binding artifact conflict, stop and record a design delta'), this must be escalated as a conflict, not resolved locally.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes. Plausible guesses include (i) 16 CSPRNG bytes like RequestId, (ii) a CVE1 digest over a RunDescriptor, (iii) a digest over the sealed evidence bundle. These have opposite consequences for the deterministic-retry golden: a random RunId is stable across nothing, a content-derived RunId collides across identical retries. Two engineers ship incompatible ledgers in week one.
escalations.blockingBecause: v1-slice.md §2.2 requires the stored-view branch to bind 'one existing sealed RunId plus manifest digest' and §7.5 requires a second process to read the sealed Run. Neither is implementable.

escalations.title: sealedManifestDigest / sealed-Run semantic manifest identity has no recipe, blocking the stored-view path
escalations.whatINeeded: How to compute the sealed Run manifest bytes and their digest, so StoredViewIntentV1.target.sealedManifestDigest can be produced and verified.
escalations.whyInsufficient: C-2 requires the field and states the rule 'Resolve RunId during request-validation and require the stored sealed-manifest bytes to match sealedManifestDigest before reading any projection or artifact' — an obligation with no defined subject. operability.v2.json lists 'sealed Run semantic manifest identity' as parked. No artifact defines the manifest's fields, canonicalization, or digest framing.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes. The manifest content set (which identities, which findings, which Coverage entries, whether ExecutionId is excluded) is exactly the kind of choice two engineers decide differently, and it is load-bearing for the required 'second-process inspection' golden and for retry determinism.
escalations.blockingBecause: v1-slice.md §7.5 and the blueprint's minimum integration golden 'second-process inspection' both require it.

escalations.title: EvidenceDigest has no byte recipe, yet the v1 exit demonstration requires evidence-commitment stability
escalations.whatINeeded: The canonical byte recipe for the analysis evidence commitment that must be byte-identical across two attempts with different ExecutionIds.
escalations.whereILooked: evidence.v1.json (the string EvidenceDigest occurs zero times), r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.4.json (8 occurrences, all as an invariant subject), operability.v2.json, resolved-inputs.v2.json, c2-plan-stage-schema.v3.json.
escalations.whyInsufficient: R-1 LN-13 asserts 'Varying ExecutionId over identical semantic inputs produces byte-identical EvidenceDigest' and coreApi says AttemptMetadata is 'Excluded from EvidenceDigest by construction' — but no artifact defines EvidenceDigest. operability.v2.json records it explicitly: surface 'EvidenceDigest byte recipe', status 'NORMATIVE-EXCLUSION-NOT-MECHANICALLY-PROVEN', blocker 'EVIDENCE binds structure but not an exact EvidenceDigest byte recipe.' evidence.v1 has no bundle-level digest at all: no bundleId, no canonical serialisation, and the string 'preimage' does not occur.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes. This is the single value the deterministic-retry golden turns on. One engineer digests the CVE1 encoding of a closed EvidenceBundle; another digests canonical JSON of a subset; another folds outcomeSetDigest with coverageId. All three pass their own tests and none interoperates.
escalations.phaseOneANote: A reasonable reader might argue this falls inside the [PHASE-1A / V10 BLOCKER] marker. The blueprint's marker text enumerates 'evaluation-proof type, verification/regeneration closure, retention policy, availability/degradation record, and purge transition' — evidence IDENTITY is not in that list, and operability.v2 tracks it as a separate parked surface. The package does not say which side of the marker it falls on. That ambiguity is itself the defect.

escalations.title: EvidenceBundle field names carry no types, and the load-bearing 'authoritative' field is missing from the schema
escalations.whatINeeded: Enough to write struct EvidenceBundle and struct EvaluationEvidence.
escalations.whyInsufficient: bundleSchema contains no 'type' key anywhere — only required/optional name lists. Diffing the schema against all 18 fixtures: 'authoritative' is used by every fixture and is the discriminator E1/E3/E7/E9 turn on, yet appears in neither required nor optional. Seven per-evaluation fields (evidenceUnits, factPartitionPinned, factPartitionRef, predicateSemanticsRef, producerDeclaredObligation, regenerationClosure, regenerationClosureRetained) appear only in fixtures. factPartitionPinned vs factPartitionRef is a redundant pair with no stated precedence. No enums are declared for verdict, completeness, privacyClass, or objects[].kind despite fixture values existing for all four. retentionPolicy has no type (fixture value 'P30D'), storageRoot has no type (fixture value '/s').
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes. An implementer building strictly from bundleSchema produces a struct in which every counterexample fixture is unrepresentable — precisely the failure mode verdictSeparation warns about ('The first draft nested verdict inside its own proof and the fixture silently validated').

escalations.title: universeCommitment recipe is under-specified and contradicts its own fixtures
escalations.whatINeeded: To recompute universeCommitment, which E1 makes a normative obligation for any authoritative clean verdict.
escalations.whyInsufficient: The algorithm is 'sha256("opensip.evidence.universe.v1" || length-prefixed sorted member keys joined)'. Length prefix width, endianness, and unit are unstated; the joiner is unstated; the domain string's own framing is unstated. memberIdentity specifies the separator \x1f while every fixture memberIds value uses '|'. Fixture commitments are 16 hexadecimal characters rather than 64, with no truncation rule. I tried six plausible framings and none reproduces sha256:5bf078b03a2a9e89.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Guaranteed. The fixtures cannot validate any correct implementation, so an implementer either abandons the golden or reverse-engineers a framing that matches a truncated digest, embedding a wrong recipe.

escalations.title: outcomeSetDigest is a required field of verdictDerivation and is never defined
escalations.whereILooked: evidence.v1.json (18 occurrences, all as a required field or a fixture value; zero definitions).
escalations.whyInsufficient: No ordering rule over outcomes, no canonicalization, no preimage, no domain separator.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes — set vs sequence semantics alone forks the value, and it is sealed into the Run.

escalations.title: SubjectSetCommitment Merkle construction has no implementable recipe
escalations.whatINeeded: Leaf framing, internal-node framing, domain separators, odd-node handling, and the non-membership proof encoding.
escalations.whereILooked: evidence.v1.json#noMatchConstruction.construction.subjectSetCommitment; IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §5 names SubjectSetCommitment as a first API.
escalations.whyInsufficient: The artifact supplies the design rationale ('A sorted-leaf Merkle tree yields NON-membership proofs from adjacent-leaf paths') and the root size (32 bytes), but no framing at any level and no hash-function statement for the tree itself.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes. Merkle framing is the classic place where two correct-looking implementations produce different roots, and the root is the durable no-match evidence.

escalations.title: subjectScopeCommitment is a required Coverage key field whose computation is owned by an unfinished surface
escalations.whatINeeded: How to compute and verify subjectScopeCommitment, required on every Coverage key.
escalations.whyInsufficient: C-2 knownLimitations states verbatim 'subjectScopeCommitment is required as a field but this contract does not say how one is computed or verified. The retention/evidence surface owns that and is REOPENED.' fact-plane knownLimitations concurs. delivery.v2's CoverageKeyV1 carries the field with a concrete fixture value (sha256:a78e6a72bb...) but no derivation.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes, and it propagates: Coverage keys are compared for exact equality across cache lookups and provider dispatch, so a divergent commitment silently changes cache behavior.
escalations.adjacency: Partially inside the V10/EVIDENCE blocker, but C-2 and FACT-PLANE are both SEAL candidates that depend on it, and the freeze §7 residual table does not name it.

escalations.title: No normative Finding type exists anywhere, and the finding fingerprint recipe is parked
escalations.whatINeeded: The shape of the 'findings' value carried by CoreCompletion::completed and projected as an exact-mode field on the reference JSON surface.
escalations.whereILooked: r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.4.json#coreCompletionSchema, fact-plane.v1.json, c2-plan-stage-schema.v3.json, evidence.v1.json, operability.v2.json#projectionParity, and a key-name search for findingSchema across the whole reachable set (zero hits).
escalations.whyInsufficient: CoreCompletion carries 'findings' and 'partialFindings' as bare names. operability.v2.json makes 'findings' one of seven requiredFields with mode 'exact' on the json reference surface, 'native' on SARIF, and 'paginated-reachable' on agent-mcp — obligations over an undefined type. operability.v2.json#knownLimitations names 'Finding fingerprint' among recipes that 'do not yet exist as exact live byte contracts'.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes. Findings are sealed into the Run, projected across five surfaces with parity obligations, and required to be byte-identical across retries. Two engineers produce incompatible Finding structs and incompatible SARIF mappings in week one.
escalations.separationFromRuleIR: This is NOT the same as the rule IR. product-dispositions.v1.json PUBLIC-RULE-IR legitimately delegates the internal rule representation to the implementer. It does not delegate the evidence-relevant result type.

escalations.title: policyOutcome.derivationDigest is required with no recipe and exactly one occurrence in the reachable set
escalations.whatINeeded: The preimage and framing for derivationDigest, a required field of the required policyOutcome on CoreCompletion.
escalations.whereILooked: r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.4.json#coreCompletionSchema.variants[0].policyOutcome (the only occurrence in any reachable artifact); evidence.v1.json#verdictDerivation.
escalations.whyInsufficient: The field is required alongside policyId and verdict. No canonicalization, preimage, domain separator, or relationship to evidence.v1's verdictDerivation is stated. R-1's rule 'the host seals using this outcome and must not re-derive a different verdict from the same inputs' makes it host-consumed and therefore cross-crate.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes. This value crosses the pure-core boundary into the sealed Run; a divergent recipe breaks retry determinism.

escalations.title: FactViewId has a wire pattern but no derivation, and it is addressable in the v1 stored-view surface
escalations.whatINeeded: How to derive factview1:sha256:<64 hex> so a stored read-fact-view query can be served.
escalations.whyInsufficient: C-2 defines only the pattern. operability.v2.json lists 'FactViewId derivation' among the six parked recipes. resolved-inputs.v2.json excludes FactViewId from PlanId without defining it.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes, and the read-fact-view operation is part of the closed stored-view query union that v1 admission must validate.

escalations.title: D9 gives no observation-to-faultCause selection rule, so one physical failure yields three defensible public error codes
escalations.whatINeeded: A rule mapping an observed host condition to exactly one faultCause.
escalations.whereILooked: d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json causeModel, codeMaps, goldenCases, nonAnalysisDerivation, concurrentConditionReducer; and delivery.v2.json#terminationIntegration.
escalations.whyInsufficient: codeMaps.rule asserts the maps are 'total and injective', which is true of cause->code, but the observation->cause step is unwritten. A ledger commit that fails with an I/O error after CAS objects were written fits durability-commit (DURABILITY.COMMIT_FAILED), cas-link (CAS.LINK_FAILED) and host-io (HOST.IO_FAILURE); goldens exist for the first two with near-identical scenario text. A SQLite failure similarly fits ledger-busy, ledger-corrupt or host-io. The reducer only says 'pick first faultCauses[0]' without specifying list order.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes. Two implementations ship different public error codes for the same crash, and public error codes are a stability surface.
escalations.versionDriftChecked: Present identically at d9-exit-contract.v1.13.json (causeSelection and observationToCause occur zero times at both versions). This is a contract gap, not version drift.

escalations.title: D9 specifies no policy for when optional HostTermination fields must be populated, and its own goldens disagree
escalations.whatINeeded: A predicate deciding when runId, executionId and coverageId are present.
escalations.whereILooked: d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json hostTerminationUnion, invariants, crossAxisInvariants, all 44 goldenCases.
escalations.whyInsufficient: nullabilityPolicy states 'Optional fields are ABSENT or present-and-valid... absence is the only way to express not-applicable', but no rule says when a field is applicable. The goldens are inconsistent for comparable events: analysis-durability-failed emits runId and executionId; analysis-cas-link-failed emits executionId only; query-required-completeness-missing emits coverageId with no runId; analysis-provider-protocol-prevents-seal emits executionId only.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes, and invariant-envelope-parity ('CommandEnvelope.termination equals process termination') makes the difference externally observable in the stable machine output that v1-slice §2.6.4 requires.

escalations.title: The normative D9 derivation lives in a retained Python checker, not in the contract; no rule produces success/policy-failed/interrupted
escalations.whyInsufficient: referenceDerivation is only {implementation: 'artifacts/check-d9.py::derive', pure: true, nonCircular: ...}. crossAxisInvariants X1/X2/X3 pin the three cause-bearing classes by biconditional; the other three classes have no derivation rule. No statement anywhere reads verdict==fail -> policy-failed; it must be inferred from exitClasses[1].meaning and one golden.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Partly mitigated by 44 goldens, but the blueprint §7.1 explicitly instructs 'Rust tests should deserialize or generate vectors from the binding JSON; do not manually copy an expected table into a second source of truth.' Here the binding JSON does not contain the function, so the port target is a Python file the implementer package never names as normative.
escalations.note: This is a package-authority question as much as a contract gap: the freeze §2 lists 'the retained check-*.py instruments' in the signed payload, so the derivation is arguably in scope — but the blueprint §5 D9 row names types and goldens, never the checker, as the source of the derivation.

escalations.title: D9 precedence between interrupted and policy-failed/success is undefined for finite commands
escalations.whatINeeded: What a finite run with verdict fail and a signal before finalization terminates as.
escalations.whereILooked: d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json crossAxisInvariants (X9 covers only commandKind==serve), finalizationTransitions, invariant-finalization-commit, all 44 goldens.
escalations.whyInsufficient: No rule, no invariant, no golden covers the combination, and invariant-finalization-commit hedges with 'Signals before it MAY yield interrupted.' The concurrentConditionReducer's inputSchema has no interruption input at all.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes, and the exit codes differ (1 vs 130) — directly user-visible in CI.

escalations.title: The sufficiency function's input type and the deficiency discriminator are undeclared, and CoverageEntry has three competing homes
escalations.whatINeeded: The 'view' type consumed by satisfy(requirement, view), the coverage enum, the rungUnavailableBecause enum, and the normative home of CoverageEntry.
escalations.whyInsufficient: The comparison logic and the first-match-wins deficiency order are mechanical, but 'view' has no schema (its shape is only inducible from 12 goldens), 'coverage' has no declared enum (only complete and unknown appear), and rungUnavailableBecause — which drives three of the five deficiency branches — is never declared and its observed values (provider-not-installed, language-tier, budget) are spelled differently from the deficiency codes they map to. The blueprint names CoverageEntry as the first API but that string occurs zero times in fact-plane.v1.json; the real candidates are C-2's 8-field coverageKey and delivery's 5-field CoverageResultV1.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes on the type signature; the 12 goldens would still pass. Two engineers agree on verdicts and disagree on the crate's public API — the classic week-one fork.

escalations.title: The implementer package pins stale artifact versions and states no rule for which version is normative
escalations.whatINeeded: To know which bytes I am building against.
escalations.whereILooked: IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md §1 and §5, IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §3, ARCHITECTURE-TO-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md §6 'Gate state per load-bearing surface'.
escalations.whyInsufficient: The blueprint's contract map links d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json, evidence.v1.json, operability.v2.json, r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.4.json and versioning-policy.v2.json. The artifacts directory heads are v1.13, v8, v10, v1.5 and v8 respectively. The same repository's plan document states in its own gate table that D9's head is v1.13 with an independent-review PASS and that v1.10/1.11/1.12 were rejected — i.e. the blueprint directs the implementer at a version the plan records as superseded three times over. d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json self-declares status 'CANDIDATE-UNREVIEWED'. Of the fifteen artifacts the blueprint links, only two (r1 v1.4, fact-identity v2) self-declare as independently reviewed and adjudicated.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes, in either direction. Building v1.6 wastes the repairs in v1.7-v1.13. Building v1.13 contradicts the only authority statement the implementer was given. The freeze §2 authority order does not resolve version selection.
escalations.blockingBecause: Nothing else can be safely started until the implementer knows which bytes are normative. This is cheap to fix and the highest-leverage single repair in the package.

escalations.title: D9 concurrent-condition golden uses an out-of-vocabulary rejection cause spelling
escalations.detail: concurrentConditionGoldens[0] ('fault-beats-rejection') carries rejectionCauses: ['invalid-config']. The closed enum spelling is 'config-invalid'. It is the only out-of-vocabulary value across all five reducer goldens. Present identically at v1.6 and v1.13.
escalations.impact: A conformance test generated directly from the artifact feeds a value the artifact's own schema rejects. Findable in an afternoon; must be escalated rather than silently corrected because the blueprint forbids choosing the easier reading.

escalations.title: delivery.v2 releaseFixtures are unusable as a test oracle
escalations.detail: Four of five releaseFixtures are valid:false with violates DL-SUPPLY or DL-PLATFORM, yet every one carries expect: 'installed', identical to the positive fixture — including reject-unlisted-platform (freebsd), reject-revoked and reject-network-verification. InstallOutcome has refused-platform / refused-revoked / refused-incomplete-set available.
escalations.impact: Almost certainly copy-paste. Do not port as vectors.

escalations.title: Blueprint §5 names first APIs that do not exist in the artifacts it links
escalations.detail: The FACT-IDENTITY row names NormalizationLevel, canonical_body_id, AnchorValidator and BudgetOutcome. In fact-identity-policy.v2.json the strings NormalizationLevel and canonicalBodyId occur zero times (the artifact uses normalisationLadder, anchorValidation, budgetModel). Similarly the FACT-PLANE row names CoverageEntry, which occurs zero times in fact-plane.v1.json.
escalations.impact: The 'First API / type' column is aspirational naming rather than extracted from the artifacts. Harmless once known, but it costs an implementer an hour per row and undermines trust in the map.

escalations.title: capabilityManifestId is a PLAN-ID-V1 input with no derivation rule
escalations.whatINeeded: How capabilityManifestId is computed, since it is PLAN-ID-V1 field 3 (release.capabilityManifestId) and DELIVERY states it enters PlanId.
escalations.whyInsufficient: manifestId has an exact derivation (sha256 over UTF8('opensip.release-manifest.v1\u0000') || JCS(manifest with manifestId and signatures omitted)). capabilityManifestId is required by ProfileEntry and enters PlanId but has no equivalent rule. The platformIds ['all-supported'] sentinel in every capability manifest also has no expansion rule.
escalations.couldAnEngineerGuessWrong: Yes — and it changes PlanId, which is otherwise the most rigorously specified value in the package. The recipe is exact; one of its inputs is not.

escalations.title: TypeScript worker supervision timeouts have no numeric values
escalations.detail: The 'host's bounded cleanup grace' after SIGINT and the wall-clock 'host-safety backstop' are both specified as concepts with no number. Everything else in the TS substrate is pinned to the byte.
escalations.impact: Two implementations differ in hard-kill timing; observable only under fault injection. Low risk but should carry a default.

escalations.title: Release expiry has no timestamp format and no offline clock-source policy
escalations.detail: createdAt / expiresAt / bundleCreatedAt have no type (RFC 3339? epoch seconds?), releaseSequence has no type, and no policy states what clock an air-gapped installer trusts when checking expiry. OfflineReleaseBundleV1 only says it 'reports metadata age/expiry'.
escalations.impact: verify_offline_bundle is ~80% writable; this is the missing fifth.

escalations.title: D9 request-rejected 'details' has no schema, yet DELIVERY requires it to carry the domain reason code
escalations.detail: hostTerminationUnion types details as {type: object, nullable: false} with no schema. delivery.v2.json#terminationIntegration requires FEATURE.REQUIRES_CAPABILITY_RUNTIME and FEATURE.EXTERNAL_SCANNER_NOT_IN_V1 to remain 'typed explanatory detail in the rejection body' without naming the field or its shape, and the golden for extension-admission-rejected populates no details at all.
escalations.impact: The excluded-form rejection is a required v1-slice §7.8 exit demonstration and a named minimum integration golden. Where the domain reason code lives on the wire is a guess.

preNamedResidualsEscalated.note: These are the escalations the litmus explicitly permits. They are recorded for completeness and do NOT count toward the failure count.

items.name: V10 / evaluation proof / retention default / custody / degradation / purge, and CD-RT-5
namedIn: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §3 EVIDENCE and TM rows UNSET-BLOCKS-FREEZE, §3.1, §5
threat-model.v3.json finding V10 UNRESOLVED and requiredProperty R4 BLOCKED-ON-EVIDENCE-AND-RETENTION
items.assessment: Consistently and honestly named across six independent locations. The package correctly forbids the implementer from choosing a default: 'Durable authoritative retention must not ship by inventing a proof/default.' I did not choose one.

items.name: ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT parked; G9 BLOCKED-NO-MECHANISM; all dependent forms reject at admission
items.assessment: Clear. The rejection path is fully specified (typed domain reason code plus D9 join), so exclusion is buildable even though the mechanism is parked.

items.name: R1-PARK-RESIDENCY — one-shot topology is the normative floor
items.assessment: Clear, and the constraint that residency may not change EvidenceDigest/PlanId/Coverage/HostTermination is stated.

items.name: R1-PARK-RUNTIME-DENIAL — static closure only; runtime authority denial NOT DISCHARGED
items.assessment: Clear and repeatedly guarded against overclaiming.

items.name: Proof and fact-custody cost measurement residual
items.assessment: Clear; explicitly does not block implementing the obligations.

items.name: FI-CORPUS-EVIDENCE — TypeScript and Rust adversarial two-producer corpora do not exist
items.assessment: Clear, and correctly framed as implementation evidence rather than an architecture hole.

items.name: Detector-pivot affordability UNMEASURED; pivot off the ordinary-analysis path; optional for v1
0/25 demonstrated; privacy/offline/platform/capacity publication BLOCKED
items.assessment: Clear, and the IMPLEMENTABLE / QUALIFIED / DEMONSTRATED separation is stated in five places. This part of the corpus is genuinely well disciplined.

sufficiencyList.finding: The identity plane is written to a standard a blind second implementer can hit. PLAN-ID-V1, SNAPSHOT-ID-V1, FACT-ID-V1 and planIntentCommitment were all reproduced byte-exactly from prose alone, first attempt, without consulting any checker. Expected preimage byte lengths matched (2500, 1080, 940, 924). This is the single strongest thing in the package and should be the template for every recipe that is still missing.

CVE1 and opensip-canonical-json-v1 are both closed, unambiguous, and correctly cross-referenced (fact-plane and snapshot-id both cite planIdContract as the normative CVE1 source rather than restating it). The 'CVE1 is an encoder after schema validation, not a permissive schema' rule prevents the obvious misuse.

Blueprint §4 crate map: 16 packages with owns / must-not-own, a dependency-direction tree, and five forbidden-edge classes declared as conformance tests from the first commit. I could write cargo-deny rules and a dependency-closure test on day one and defend every edge.

The host/pure-core boundary is decided, argued and closed. CoreDeps is a closed four-field record with a seven-item forbids list and an explicit anti-extension rule; the factoring rationale (C-2's no-effect-authority stages are exactly the pure-core stages) means the boundary is derivable rather than arbitrary. §3.1's list of host-owned effects is complete enough to route any new capability without asking.

C-2 PlanIntent is a genuinely closed tagged union with exactTopLevelFields per variant, a validationTotality clause defined over every parsed JSON value including hostile wrong-type nesting ('Validation never raises a language/runtime exception for caller-controlled parsed JSON'), regex-pinned wireTypes for every scalar, and 35 + 14 + 13 fixtures. validate_plan_intent is writable Monday morning.

The identity allocation lifecycle is unambiguous and consistent across four documents: RequestId at trusted ingress before parsing, then closed PlanIntent validation and commitment, then ExecutionId at attempt admission, then SnapshotId, then PlanId, then RunId at seal. Blueprint §2's explicit warning that 'admit -> PlanId' must NOT be implemented as allocating an attempt before request validation is exactly the kind of anti-guidance a package should carry.

REQUEST-ID-V1 is complete: 16 CSPRNG bytes, exact regex, allocation point ahead of every named downstream step, the four request classes it covers, the rule that allocation does not admit an attempt, the entropy-boundary justification, and the custody/exclusion rules. No guesses.

The TypeScript provider substrate is the best-specified protocol in the package: byte-exact framing, RFC 8949 core deterministic CBOR with a closed 9-type model and 7 forbidden constructs, a closed frame envelope with per-direction sequence discipline, 16 frame types with terminal flags, 16 closed payload schemas, 11 numeric limits, a 7-phase ordering FSM, exact argv and a closed environment spec (inheritParent false, LC_ALL=C, LANG=C, TZ=UTC, 13 vars unset, extras forbidden), an explicit admitOn condition and DISCARD_ALL_CANDIDATES otherwise, and a self-digest so drift is detectable. Two engineers would interoperate.

threat-model.v3 storageNamespace is implementation-grade: 12 exact paths, objectId-to-path derivation with an explicit prohibition on using the colon-bearing wire form as a filename, handle-relative no-follow opens with 'String-prefix checks are insufficient', a collision rule that treats digest mismatch as corruption and never overwrites, per-project SQLite tenancy, a single authority-selection record with compare-and-swap, and complete purge and migration state machines with crash-recovery tables and fixtures.

The pre-first-durable-write obligation is answerable without guessing: a closed detection result set, three exposure classes, a closed admissionDecisions table with REFUSE / REQUIRE-EXPLICIT-POLICY / DO-NOT-CLAIM-SAFE outcomes, a signed 4-entry detector catalog, the scoping rule that NOT-DETECTED is never global safety, and V18's requirement to revalidate handles every run rather than trusting admission-time checks.

The D9 exit map and HostTermination union are fully writable today. The design choice of forbidding exitCode from the payload so class and code can never disagree, plus the absence-not-null policy, plus deny-unknown-fields, produce a Rust enum that is safe by construction.

CI layer-4 behavior is decided (product-dispositions A1-RI-04 CI_IGNORES_LAYER_4, explicitly superseding the provisional posture in resolved-inputs), stated identically in three package documents, and mechanically enforced inside the PlanId recipe itself — a layer-4 record under ci is PLAN_ID_PROFILE_VIOLATION, and I reproduced the local-interactive keyed variant's digest. Presence is not an admission failure; that nuance is stated.

The fact plane's relation registry is concrete: 12 relations, each with a layer and a totally ordered ladder, a dependsOn table, and a parallel 12-entry closed payload schema registry with named enums, universeRule, and per-rung required/forbidden field sets. The closed 5-value deficiency vocabulary and its first-match-wins resolution order are stated, as is the anti-tier rule that layer 'carries no ordering' and that quality/tier/degraded/rank are forbidden field names — C-1 is enforced structurally, not editorially.

The excluded-form rejection joins are closed and correctly non-interchangeable: FEATURE.REQUIRES_CAPABILITY_RUNTIME and FEATURE.EXTERNAL_SCANNER_NOT_IN_V1 remain domain detail, both map to rejectionCause extension-admission-rejected and public EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED, with the explicit rule that a DELIVERY spelling outside D9's closed vocabulary is a contract defect rather than a new local code. This is stated identically in the blueprint, the freeze and delivery.v2.

The release supply chain is implementable: an 8-step admissionOrder, the exact signed-bytes formula UTF8('opensip.release-manifest.v1\u0000') || JCS(manifest minus manifestId and signatures), manifestId = sha256(signedBytes), Ed25519 per RFC 8032, keyId derivation, hardcoded role thresholds (root 2-of-3, release 2-of-3, delegated-artifact 1-of-2), non-TOFU root pinning, rotation signed by both old and new thresholds, a closed OfflineReleaseBundleV1, and a closed 9-value InstallOutcome enum.

The internal rule IR is legitimately delegated, not accidentally missing. product-dispositions.v1.json PUBLIC-RULE-IR states 'The rule IR may be an internal versioned implementation contract, but v1 makes no public compatibility promise', and blueprint §4 gives crates/rules a clear must-not-own list. An implementer can design it freely. This is a genuine and well-marked delegation and should not be corrected.

The package is consistently honest about what it has not established. 'implementable: true, a green checker, or this scope decision is not DISCHARGED or DEMONSTRATED evidence' appears in five documents; the freeze is explicitly marked NOT DECLARED with placeholder signers; blueprint §8.3 separates IMPLEMENTABLE / QUALIFIED / DEMONSTRATED; every artifact carries knownLimitations naming its own authorship and review state. Several of the escalations above were findable only because the corpus documents its own gaps. That discipline is the reason this litmus could be run at all.

verdict.criterion: ARCHITECTURE-TO-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md §1.3 / G5: an implementer must escalate only items already named as residuals or parks. IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §8 restates it: 'They may escalate only a named residual or a detected conflict with a binding artifact.'
verdict.statement: The package fails its own litmus. Twenty escalations of BLOCKING or FORK severity are not named as residuals or parks anywhere in the four implementer-facing documents. The failure is NOT the V10/retention hole — that one item is named consistently in six places and I did not have to guess about it. The failure clusters in three places the package presents as settled: (1) the identity recipes below the Run — RunId, sealed-Run manifest identity, EvidenceDigest, Finding fingerprint, FactViewId, subjectScopeCommitment — which operability.v2.json itself records as 'do not yet exist as exact live byte contracts' but which appear in no residual table, and one of which IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6.6 positively asserts exists; (2) the Rust provider protocol, whose specification is orphaned from every reachable path in the package; and (3) the D9 derivation's back half — observation-to-cause selection, optional-field presence, and the success/policy-failed/interrupted branch — which the contract delegates to a Python checker the implementer package never names as normative.
verdict.importantQualifier: This is a fail on package completeness, not a judgement that the architecture is wrong. The identity plane, the crate factoring, the core boundary, the TypeScript substrate, the storage layout and the admission ordering are of high quality and several are exemplary. Three of the five BLOCKING items (ESC-01, ESC-18, and probably ESC-02/ESC-03 by transitive reference) look like packaging and cross-referencing defects rather than missing architecture — the artifacts may well already exist at heads the blueprint does not link.
verdict.notADeclaration: This record declares no seal, no freeze, no product acceptance, and no disposition of any surface. It is one blind implementer's readiness assessment.

establishes: That a competent Rust engineer, given only the delivered package, either can or cannot reach a specific design decision without inventing architecture — measured decision by decision, not in aggregate.

That four normative byte recipes (PLAN-ID-V1, SNAPSHOT-ID-V1, FACT-ID-V1, planIntentCommitment) are reproducible by an independent implementation from prose alone, because I did it and matched the vectors exactly. This is real, transferable evidence about those four contracts.

That one stated recipe (evidence.v1 universeCommitment) is NOT reproducible from its own text against its own fixtures, because I tried six framings and failed. This is a concrete defect, not an opinion.
That specific artifacts are unreachable from the package's own link graph, verified by exhaustive substring search across all four documents.
Where the package's cross-references, versions and asserted facts disagree with each other.
doesNotEstablish: That the architecture is correct, safe, performant, or a good product. A package can be perfectly implementable and describe a bad system.
That the contracts I could NOT reach are wrong. rust-provider-protocol.v4.json is 124 KB and may be excellent; my finding is only that the package does not lead an implementer to it.
That the versions the blueprint links are the versions the architecture owners intend. ESC-18 is precisely the observation that I cannot tell.

That my escalations would survive contact with the deliberation history. Several may already have written dispositions in review artifacts I was required not to read — but that is the point of the litmus: if the answer is only in the argument history, the delivered package has not delivered it.

That the sufficiency findings would survive implementation. 'I could write this struct' is weaker than 'this struct is right'. Every SUFFICIENT verdict here means implementable-from-the-text, never demonstrated, qualified, or correct.

Anything about the concurrently-reviewed retention-tiers.v22 or evidence.v8, which I deliberately did not read. If either supplies the missing evidence identity recipes, several FORK escalations collapse into ESC-18 (version drift) — which would be a much cheaper fix than it currently appears.
That a checker passing, or this document existing, upgrades any claim. Per the corpus's own rule, IMPLEMENTABLE is not QUALIFIED and is not DEMONSTRATED.
whatABlindPassDoesAndDoesNotEstablish.singleMostUsefulNextStep: Resolve ESC-18 first. Publishing one table that names, for each of the eleven load-bearing surfaces, the exact filename and SHA-256 an implementer must build against — and adding the four orphaned artifacts (rust-provider-protocol, trusted-request-context, and the two join artifacts) to the blueprint §5 map — would let this litmus be re-run against the intended bytes. Several of the twenty unnamed escalations may not survive that.
